inputs.task:
You are one seat in a structured forecasting panel. You have exactly
one job, defined below. Obey these laws before any instruction in
your job text:

1. PACKET-ONLY FACTS. Every fact, stat, price, quote, or date you
   state must come from the context you were given. Anything else —
   memory, general knowledge, plausible inference stated as fact — is
   FABRICATION and fails the entire exam. If the packet does not
   contain something, write it under "could_not_read" and reason
   without it. Never fill a gap.
2. OUTPUT IS ONE JSON OBJECT, matching the shape your job text gives,
   and nothing else: no prose outside the JSON, no markdown fences.
3. Every claim carries a ref. A claim without a ref does not ship.
4. Your distribution is over the moneyline only: {"A": p, "B": 1-p},
   each in [0, 1], summing to 1.
5. You are being graded against settled ground truth you cannot see.
   There is no audience and no reward for confidence; a calibrated
   number with honest gaps beats a bold number built on air.

JOB: STYLES, Round 1 — POSITION.
Your read is the interaction, not the fighters separately: style
classifications, the stance pass (same-stance or southpaw/orthodox —
what that does to each fighter's favorite weapons), the weapon-on-habit
map (each fighter's signature weapons against the other's documented
habits and defensive liabilities), and the neutralization test: name
each fighter's primary path to victory, then judge from the packet
whether the other has demonstrated neutralizing that path. Grade the
fight that remains if the key strength is neutralized.

CONTEXT: {"card_slot": "Co-main event \u2014 lightweight", "date": "2026-10-10", "lock_basis": "T-30min before the main card (8:00 PM ET start)", "name": "UFC Fight Night 290: Allen vs. Duncan (UFC Vegas 122)", "rounds": 3, "venue": "Meta APEX, Las Vegas, NV", "weight_class": "Lightweight"} {"A": "Matheus Camilo", "B": "Jai Herbert"} {"fighters": {"A": {"finish_profile": "5 of 11 wins by KO; 4 finishes in round one", "physical": {"age": 25, "height": "5-10", "reach_in": 69.5, "stance": "Orthodox"}, "style_line": {"defensive_liability": "Was submitted by rear-naked choke in his UFC debut; striking volume is too low to win rounds that stay standing against a longer man", "pace_profile": "Young pressure fighter; first UFC co-main event", "primary": "Wrestle-grinder \u2014 a BJJ brown belt whose UFC game runs through 4.16 takedowns per 15", "secondary": "Opportunistic power (first-round KO of Sadykhov)", "signature_weapons": ["Takedown chains behind modest striking (2.22 SLpM at 43%)"], "style_adjusted_read": "The 2.22 SLpM is genuinely low, not a counter-striker's design \u2014 read flat, with the wrestling as the entire round-winning plan"}, "technique_tendency": {"favorite_counters": "Could-Not-Read", "stance_record_vs_opposite": "Same-stance pairing (both orthodox) \u2014 mirrored read applies", "tendencies": ["Tests with low kicks early (observed pattern is post-fight \u2014 excluded); pre-fight read: uses wrestling to make fights a grind (realcombatmedia keys)"]}}, "B": {"finish_profile": "10 KO wins in 14; former Cage Warriors lightweight champion; BJJ black belt", "physical": {"age": 38, "height": "6-1", "reach_in": 77, "stance": "Orthodox"}, "style_line": {"defensive_liability": "67% takedown defense against a 4.16-per-15 wrestler is the whole fight; has been stopped by elite pressure (Topuria, Moicano)", "pace_profile": "At 38, his cleanest path is an early finish; output fades are the career pattern the keys game-plan around", "primary": "Long range striker \u2014 fights at the end of a 7.5-inch reach advantage", "secondary": "Veteran shot selection with real one-shot power (0.84 knockdowns per 15)", "signature_weapons": ["Left hook to the body \u2014 named as his favorite weapon by realcombatmedia's film study", "Jab at range"], "style_adjusted_read": "His striking rates are modest but they are earned over 10 UFC fights against better opposition than Camilo has faced; the reach makes his 3.19 SLpM play bigger than the number"}, "technique_tendency": {"favorite_counters": "Could-Not-Read by trigger; the body hook is his named favorite weapon", "stance_record_vs_opposite": "Same-stance pairing (both orthodox) \u2014 mirrored read: whose lead weapons collide in the pocket, and Herbert's length decides it", "tendencies": ["Keeps fights at the end of his jab, stays off the fence (pre-fight keys)", "Punishes low-accuracy strikers \u2014 Camilo lands 43%"]}}}}

Your brief names: who imposes their fight, who dictates location and
pace, the two or three technique collisions that decide this matchup,
and your neutralization verdict. Anything the packet's style or
technique sections mark Could-Not-Read goes under could_not_read —
do not reconstruct a fighter's tendencies from reputation. Close with
your moneyline distribution, driven by the interaction read: if the
neutralization holds, price the fight that remains, not the fighters'
résumés.

Return exactly:
{"seat": "STYLES", "round": 1, "status": "ok",
 "brief": "<your read>",
 "claims": [{"claim": "...", "ref": "..."}],
 "could_not_read": ["..."],
 "distribution": {"A": 0.0, "B": 0.0},
 "state_pull": null}
